name: Sonepiprazole
summary: Sonepiprazole is a highly selective dopamine D4 receptor antagonist of the phenylpiperazine family.

pharmacology.text: Sonepiprazole (INN; developmental code names U-101387 and PNU-101387) is a highly selective dopamine D4 receptor antagonist of the phenylpiperazine family. In animals, unlike D2 receptor antagonists like haloperidol, sonepiprazole does not block the behavioral effects of amphetamine or apomorphine, does not alter spontaneous locomotor activity on its own, and lacks extrapyramidal and neuroendocrine effects.

uses.text: Sonepiprazole was investigated as an antipsychotic for the treatment of schizophrenia in a placebo-controlled clinical trial, but in contrast to olanzapine, no benefits were found, and it was not researched further for this use. It was under development by Pharmacia Corporation for the treatment of schizophrenia, and reached phase 2 clinical trials for this indication, but development was discontinued in March 2001.
